findings.checklist_item: Add a behavioral-equivalence check (e.g. a small verdict-parity run over the same corpus comparing inline-digest vs hoisted-reference judge outputs, or an explicit rationale/spot-eval that the cross-block reference is read equivalently) and correct the 'identical bytes, moved' framing to acknowledge the query-side slot is a reference substitution, not a byte-preserving move.
evidence: Plan: 'The relocation is therefore never worse — identical bytes, moved from an unbillable-as-prefix block to a cacheable one.'

Plan (user ordering): 'the QUERY TICKET DIGEST given in your system prompt' is substituted into the FIRST/SECOND slot — i.e. a pointer replaces the inline digest block, so the user-message bytes are NOT identical to today for the query side.

overlap_judge.md:11-15 reads TWO inline digests positionally: 'You are given TWO ticket digests in a fixed order — call them FIRST and SECOND … read DIRECTIONALLY as "FIRST <relation> SECOND"'. The model must now resolve a pointer to another block rather than read an inline digest.

The cited precedent prompts.py:438-463 (resolve_prompt_cached) is a pure stable/volatile SPLIT that does not change what the model reads, so it does not underwrite 'never worse' for behavior — only for the pure-split cases.

All plan tests assert on request bytes (system_prompt/instructions) and token counts; none assert judge verdicts (relation/confidence/shared_artifact) are unchanged versus the inline-digest baseline. The judge prompt itself states 'false flags are costly'.
findings.finding: The plan's 'never worse — identical bytes, moved' claim is inaccurate and its behavioral-equivalence assumption is untested: the AFTER user block replaces the query digest with a cross-block reference pointer, a semantic input change to a precision-sensitive judge that no test validates leaves verdicts unchanged.
findings.location: Approach section ('The relocation is therefore never worse — identical bytes'); Testing/Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: A candidate that today gets a confident directional/duplicate verdict is judged differently after the hoist because the model treats the referenced (not inline) query digest with less weight, silently changing which overlap findings are surfaced.
The AFTER token-measurement run shows the cache win but a precision regression goes unnoticed because no output-equivalence check exists.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact '<one-line orientation>' system-prompt string AND how the base overlap-judge prompt's 'you are given TWO ticket digests … call them FIRST and SECOND' framing is reconciled with one digest now living in the system block, so the directional 'FIRST <relation> SECOND' reading is preserved for the substituted reference slot in BOTH orderings.
evidence: overlap_judge.md:11-13 states 'You are given TWO ticket digests in a fixed order — call them FIRST and SECOND. Decide the relationship of FIRST to SECOND'

judge.py:60 resolves the base prompt via resolve_prompt(prompt, {}); the plan appends the query digest AFTER this, so the base prompt text (asserting both digests are co-located and read as FIRST/SECOND) is unchanged and now contradicts the new message shape

The plan's layout sketch shows 'QUERY TICKET DIGEST — <one-line orientation>' in the system block and 'the QUERY TICKET DIGEST given in your system prompt' in the user slot, but the actual orientation string is a placeholder and never specified

The prompt's directional decision rule ('FIRST <relation> SECOND', relations supersedes/depends_on) is order-sensitive; correctness now hinges on the model mapping the reference slot to the system-prompt digest, which no prompt text instructs
findings.finding: The overlap-judge base prompt still tells the model both digests arrive together in the user message, but the plan hoists the query digest into the system prompt without reconciling that framing, and leaves the load-bearing 'one-line orientation' / reference-slot wiring unspecified — an instruction-locality gap the directional 'FIRST <relation> SECOND' semantics depend on.
findings.location: Approach (system/user layout sketch) and Scope ('a module-private helper builds the augmented system prompt'); vs src/rebar/llm/reviewers/overlap_judge.md:11-13
scenarios: Ordering 2 puts the reference in the SECOND slot; if the model treats the system-prompt digest as always 'the query' regardless of slot, the directional label inverts and aggregate() emits a rebar link command with source/target swapped
The model, told in the body it will be 'given TWO ticket digests' in the user turn, may ignore or mis-bind the system-prompt digest
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope an explicit edit to overlap_judge.md (or the helper's appended header) that (a) names the system digest as one of the two ordered participants and (b) instructs the model to treat 'the QUERY TICKET DIGEST given in your system prompt' as occupying whichever FIRST/SECOND slot the user message places it in; and give the verbatim orientation string rather than a placeholder.

findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing capability claim — that claude-sonnet-4-6's real prompt-cache prefix floor is 1024 tokens — directly contradicts the codebase's operative constant CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096 (documented as the Opus 4.8 floor), and is grounded only in narrative prose describing a two-call probe rather than a recorded, reproducible measurement artifact on the ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note that warn_if_cache_ineffective is gated on input_tokens>=4096 and therefore stays dark for the ~1,024-token overlap-judge prefix, and state how a future silent caching regression at this call site would be detected (or accept the blind spot explicitly).
evidence: structured_run.py:421 `and usage.get("input_tokens", 0) >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` — the ineffective-cache warning is suppressed below 4096.
Plan: post-move prefix 'measures ~1,024 tokens ... at the boundary', i.e. well below 4096, so these calls fall in the suppressed band.
The plan relies on a one-off BEFORE/AFTER manual measurement to confirm caching works, with no standing signal for regressions on this call path.
findings.finding: Because the post-move prefix (~1,024 tokens) sits below the codebase's CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096, the in-repo cache-effectiveness observability (warn_if_cache_ineffective, gated on input_tokens >= 4096) will never fire for the overlap-judge call site, so a silent runtime caching failure for these exact calls would go unwarned — the plan does not name this observability blind spot.
scenarios: Post-ship, a prompt edit drifts the overlap-judge prefix below the true sonnet floor and caching silently reverts to zero; no warning fires because input_tokens is under 4096, so the cost bleed is invisible.
